note: kind: 'own' = you buy it. 'rent' = hourly from a provider. Prices in USD unless currency says EUR. See CONTRIBUTING.md before adding an entry.

hardware.label: 2x DGX Spark
hardware.notes: Efficiency and batching calibrated against the published MiaAI-Lab decode bench: 82.4 tok/s single stream, 120.4 aggregate / 33.6 per stream at concurrency 4 (peak aggregate 134.6 at x3). Prefill is an order of magnitude below HBM systems.

hardware.label: DGX Station GB300
hardware.notes: Calibrated against an operator run: 59.59 tok/s single stream, 571-652 aggregate with 10 agents at 262K context, HBM-only, zero preemption. 748 GB total but only 252 GB is HBM3e - a model that spills into the LPDDR5X tier loses roughly an order of magnitude on decode.

hardware.label: 2x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell
hardware.notes: Price estimated: sub-8-GPU configurations are far less standardised than HGX. A community DeepSeek run measured 28.5% efficiency and 1.66x batching — not applied; the Qwen3.6 bf16 single-stream yardstick (~218 tok/s on one card) is consistent with keeping efficiency near 0.06 for the bandwidth-estimate path. Prefer matched profiles (deepseek-rtxpro-community, qwen36-rtxpro2-nvfp4) over the estimate when the model matches.

hardware.label: 4x RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell
hardware.notes: Sized on the model rather than the catalogue: 8 GPUs would leave three quarters of the memory unused. No NVLink, so all-reduce runs over PCIe - one reason TP=4 is preferable to TP=8.

hardware.label: 4x H200
hardware.notes: Hopper: no FP4 tensor cores, so weights double. Lead times reported at 30-50 weeks. Included to quantify the cost of buying the previous generation, not as a recommendation. The gptoss-h200-fp8 profile (derived from TRT-LLM H200 FP8 offline max-throughput) is far above the 0.05×6 estimate; efficiency/batching stay conservative for non-profile models because those tables are synthetic short-context peaks, not realistic traffic.

hardware.label: 1x B300 (288 GB)
hardware.notes: 288 GB on one GPU means no tensor parallelism at all. 1,400 W per GPU: air cooling is not viable, direct liquid cooling is mandatory, which is why infrastructure cost is more than double the other nodes. NVIDIA does not publish retail pricing - the ~$53k GPU figure is a market estimate. gptoss-b300-fp4 is derived from B200 TRT-LLM tables (B300 ≠ B200); leave efficiency at 0.05 for the estimate path and use the matched profile when sizing gpt-oss.

hardware.label: 4x B300 (1,152 GB)
hardware.topology: TP=4 / EP=4 over NVLink (NVIDIA Qwen3.5 deploy shape)
hardware.notes: Multi-GPU B300 node matching NVIDIA's minimum validated footprint for Qwen3.5-397B-A17B NVFP4 (4× B200/B300/GB200/GB300). Memory and bandwidth are 4× the 1x B300 catalogue row; price/infra scaled from the single-GPU estimate (not a vendor quote). Direct liquid cooling mandatory. Prefer the matched Qwen3.5 profile when sizing that model.

hardware.label: 4x H200 - OVHcloud (EU)
hardware.notes: h200-4-gpu: 900 GiB RAM, 94 vCPU, 12.5 TB disk, 20 Gbps. VAT excluded. GDPR, 99.99% SLA.

hardware.label: HGX B300 8x - Scaleway (EU)
hardware.notes: The only Blackwell you can rent inside the EU today. Sold as an 8-GPU node only: for a model that needs 142 GB this is sixteen times the required capacity. Hourly figure derived from an aggregator (~$8.54/GPU-hour), not from Scaleway's published price list - verify before quoting.

hardware.label: 4x RTX PRO 6000 - RunPod (US)
hardware.notes: NOT a compliant option under data-residency constraints. Included to size the sovereignty premium.

hardware.label: 1x B300 - RunPod (US)
hardware.notes: NOT compliant under data-residency constraints. The cheapest configuration in either catalogue that hosts a 142 GB model comfortably - which is precisely the point about what Europe cannot rent yet.
